# Exaptation Studio

Exaptation Studio is the venture studio of LGI Sustainable Innovation. It builds and tests ventures by repurposing European R&D, sustainability expertise and existing technologies.

Official website: https://exaptation.studio/
Contact: thomas@exaptation.studio
Parent organisation: LGI Sustainable Innovation — https://lgi.earth/

## Green Claims Fix

French page: https://exaptation.studio/fr/green-claims-fix/
English page: https://exaptation.studio/en/green-claims-fix/

Green Claims Fix helps consumer-facing brands review environmental marketing claims, identify which claims need attention, determine what evidence should support them, identify evidence gaps, and prepare clearer evidence-aligned wording and actions.

Primary market: France and the European Union.
Primary scope: business-to-consumer commercial communications such as websites, product pages, packaging, advertising, campaigns and marketplace listings.
Typical users: consumer brands, ecommerce companies, marketing teams, sustainability teams and product teams.

### Service levels

Bronze / Quick Fix — EUR 39: focused review of up to 5 priority claims. It explains why each claim deserves attention, links the relevant official source or rule, identifies evidence to collect or request, and recommends the next action.

Silver / Green Claims Fix — EUR 249 (called Argent in French): structured review of up to 25 priority claims. It maps claims to available evidence, identifies what is supported and what is still missing, prepares supplier evidence requests, suggests clearer evidence-aligned wording and provides a Green Claims Evidence Pack.

Gold / Expert Review — from EUR 1,490: includes the Silver review plus human expert review of priority claims and supporting documents, a consolidated action file, a review call and a recheck after modifications.

Green Claims Fix supports claim review, substantiation preparation and remediation. It is not legal advice, certification or assurance.

Regulatory focus includes current French consumer law and Directive (EU) 2024/825 (Empowering Consumers for the Green Transition / ECGT). The separate Green Claims Directive proposal COM(2023) 166 should not be confused with Directive (EU) 2024/825.

Key concepts: green claims, environmental claims, greenwashing risk, environmental marketing compliance, claim substantiation, evidence readiness, Directive (EU) 2024/825, ECGT, UCPD, France, European Union.
